the homogenization treatment of the as-cast Mg-14Li-0.5Ni alloy causes the transformation of the bcc structure to an hcp structure
The FFT shows that the matrix is still bcc-structured and that the spherical particles have an hcp structure (α phase).
There were spherical phases with an average size of 350 nm in the matrix. ... the spherical particles have an hcp structure (α phase).

phases_and_microstructures.name: continuous alpha-phase layer at grain boundary

evidence.quote: the layers of the α phase almost fully separate and surround the grains of the β phase. Further careful observation showed that the contact angle between the α phase and β phase is zero, which indicates that the grain boundary is completely wetting
The alloy undergoes complete dynamic recrystallization after rolling at room temperature, and the average grain size is approximately 0.4 μm.
The recrystallized grain size is significantly reduced to 80 nm, and the distribution of grain size is shown in the inset of Fig. 2b.
an α phase with a size of 50 nm was also detected, which is marked by a red arrow in Fig. 2b.

in the rolled alloy, there is no continuous layer between α and β (Fig. 2d), the grain boundary becomes incomplete wetting, which indicates the transition from complete to incomplete wetting appeared during the rolling process.

the increase in strength is mainly caused by the boundaries between α and β hindering the movement of dislocations.

The α phase introduced by homogenization has a higher ability to produce dislocations than the matrix [11,12] , compared with the as-cast alloy, the homogenized alloy can produce more dislocations to adapt continuous deformation, thus, the uniform elongation is improved.
the evenly distributed α phase disperses the stress of the matrix during plastic deformation, thereby avoiding the stress concentration of the coarse grains and improving the ductility.

mechanisms.name: dynamic recrystallization nucleation at alpha/beta boundaries

evidence.quote: the boundaries between α and β provide a large number of nucleation sites for recrystallized grains, thereby reducing the driving force required for recrystallization and promoting the nucleation of dynamically recrystallized grains [18] .

both nucleation and motion of dislocations are suppressed in the nanograined sample [19] , and there are not enough dislocations to adapt to the subsequent strain, so the nanostructured sample exhibits higher strength and lower plasticity compared with the ultrafine-grained sample.
